name: Redwood
lede: Redwood is a muted brownish red in the ISCC-NBS dictionary; it is also the name of a dyewood family, and the books tie the word to the dye more than to the tree.

sections.title: Two meanings
sections.body: As a swatch, Redwood is the ISCC-NBS 1955 dictionary name for a grayish red, and Maerz and Paul had recorded it in 1917 [2]. It sits close to [[red]], with a brown cast like [[brown]] and [[rust]] [2]. Separately, redwood is a dye term: a conservation paper of 1986, cited in the Pigment Compendium bibliography, covers tests for quinone, lichen and redwood dyestuffs [1].

sections.title: What the dye name tells us
sections.body: That citation shows only that conservators treat redwood dyes as a recognised group [1]. Our books do not say which woods are meant, so this article does not claim more [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Redwood is a fairly common muted red in painting: it appears in 1.09% of the archive (259 paintings), more common than 67% of the named colors, as photographed [3]. It peaks in the 1400s at 2.3 times the expected rate, and most often plays an accent [3]. It is notably over-represented in Indian paintings, at 2.5 times [3].

origin.named_after: origin undocumented in our sources (a tree and a dye group share the word)
